protocol_checks.vulnerability_mechanism: CONFIRMED: with --sleep-idle-seconds enabled, server_res_generator::wait_until_no_sleep() releases mutex_tasks after observing !sleeping without retaining an active-handler reference. start_loop() can then enter sleep and server_context_impl::destroy() resets llama_init, freeing the model-owned llama_vocab, while the HTTP worker continues through the cached ctx_server.vocab pointer. The patch repository's proposed fix adds the missing active-request lifetime guard and nulls vocab, matching this race/UAF mechanism.
protocol_checks.atomic_bic: CONFIRMED: e6ab62c4a1af57fcba5c982ced53c2522b9517d1 is the smallest public first-write that adds llama_init.reset() to destroy() while leaving the cached vocab pointer unchanged. Earlier PR members establish sleep/wait and destroy scaffolding, but do not free llama_init there; later members cannot be the first write.
protocol_checks.immediate_parent_absence: CONFIRMED: the BIC has the single parent 44a5a26c32ec7d41706680a4d2ca1f268c9166a2. In that parent, destroy() frees mctx, slot state, and batch state but does not reset llama_init; vocab is still assigned from llama_model_get_vocab(model). The UAF-producing model free is therefore absent from the immediate parent.
protocol_checks.squash_member_decomposition: CONFIRMED: PR #18228 exposes a linear 14-member chain from e1d7b43409436682a8adf77ff2b95ad7a7bcc9df through 06a5ebe187caa458ea8f1d865e744e8b31f58ef4. The master landing ddcb75dd8ac42dc23eb84f13bb17670fe9f2d49b is a one-parent GitHub squash whose message aggregates those members, so it is not the atomic BIC. The misleading member 105e2f3cf67cf726e9ea9761faf4c1bdd824370d titled 'fix use-after-free' only gates metrics.init() on !is_resume and does not repair this vocab race.

GitHub comparison reports that b9060 (ad092246587b16299291056a78bf6f73f636f114) and b9445 (af6528e6df5d798f7f1363ec1141699be0f638e2) are descendants of that landing, with ddcb75dd as their merge base.
